intro_html: Chile verde is that tangy, green, slow-simmered chicken that makes people ask for your recipe. Thighs keep it juicy, tomatillos and green chiles do the heavy lifting on flavor, and it stays high protein and cheap per serving. One batch makes 14 servings.
cost_closing_html: About $4.19 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings runs about 52g protein for roughly 557 calories, at around $2.44 a bowl.
upsell_html: One pot of this and you will look forward to lunch instead of dreading it. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Go with boneless skinless thighs here. They are cheaper than breast and stay tender through a long cook.
Fresh tomatillos are usually cents on the dollar in season, so buy them when they are cheap.
Canned diced green chiles save you the roasting and peeling, and they cost next to nothing.
make_it: Husk and quarter the tomatillos, then lay them in the crock with the chicken thighs.
Add the chopped onion and both cans of green chiles.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours until the chicken pulls apart easily.
Shred the thighs and stir them back into the green sauce.
Cook up your rice and steam the broccoli.
Serve the chile verde over rice with broccoli on the side.
